summary: Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with the provisions of the Power Supply Agreement dated 5.1.2011 and Power Purchase Agreement dated 25.3.2011 for directions to make Energy Charges as pass-through based on the actual fuel cost incurred by the Petitioner. This order is passed in compliance with the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in judgment dated 27.02.2026 in Civil Appeal Nos. 2584-2585 of 2026 titled _West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. v. Adhunik Power & Natural Resources Ltd. & Ors_ .), whereby the Commission has been directed to modify its consequential order dated 11.02.2026, passed in terms of the judgment of Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (“the APTEL”) dated 04.09.2025 in Appeal Nos. 143/2020 & 66/2022, in terms of directions contained therein. 2. The Petitioner, Adhunik Power and Natural Resources Limited (in short, “APNRL”), had filed this Petition under Section 79 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”) read with Article 10 of the Power Sale Agreement (“PSA”) dated 05.01.2011 executed between Respondent No. 2 and Respondent No. 1, and the Power Purchase Agreement (“PPA”) dated 25.03.2011 entered into with Respondent No. 2, seeking directions to the Respondents to make energy charges as pass through based on the actual fuel cost incurred by the Petitioner on account of Change in Law events arising from (i) shortfall in supply of coal under tapering linkage granted pending operationalisation of Ganeshpur captive coal block, and (ii) cancellation of Ganeshpur captive coal block allocation. 4. Aggrieved by the Commission’s aforesaid order, both APNRL and WBSEDCL approached the APTEL through Appeal Nos. 143/2020 and 66/2020, respectively. The APTEL, _vide_ common judgment dated 04.09.2025, affirmed the findings of the Commission that (i) Ganeshpur captive coal block was the recognised source of fuel under the PPA/PSA, and (ii) APNRL was entitled to compensation to the extent of shortfall in tapering linkage granted pending operationalisation of the captive block, which it met through the e-auction or import of coal, etc. (albeit the APTEL disagreed with the direction to approach through a fresh Petition). However, the APTEL overturned the Commission’s findings on coal block cancellation and held that the cancellation of allotment of Ganeshpur captive coal block in pursuance of the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s Judgment in _Manohar Lal Sharma v. Principal Secy. & Ors_ ., constituted a Change in Law event in terms of Article 10.1.1(b) of the PSA/PPA. The APTEL also held that _90. The Commission has, thus, fallen into grave error in not recognizing the Coal Block Deallocation Judgment of the Supreme Court as a Change in Law event in this case in terms of Article 10.1.1(b) of the PPA._ _100. We also hold that cancellation of allotment of Ganeshpur captive coal block in pursuance to the Coal Block Deallocation Judgment of the Supreme Court, constitute Change in Law event in terms of Article 10.1(b) of the PPA/PSA executed between the parties._ _compensation to the extent of shortfall in Tapering Linkage granted to it pending operationalization of the captive coal block, which it met through e-auction or import of coal etc. for generation of electricity in its power project and supply of the same to WBSEDCL. However, we do not agree with the direction of the Commission that the petitioner should approach the Commission through a fresh petition in this regard giving details of Tapering Linkage granted to it and the details of coal requirement met through e- auction, imported coal etc. to meet the shortfall of the coal in the Tapering Linkage._ 5. In terms of the above directions, the matter was taken up for hearing on 18.09.2025, 14.10.2025, 25.11.2025, and 23.12.2025, and after considering the submissions of the parties as well as the information/details furnished by them, the Commission passed the consequential order on 11.02.2026. attributed to APNRL and accordingly, set aside the findings of the APTEL to the limited extent that it granted compensation for procurement of coal through e-auction/import to meet shortfall in tapering linkage granted pending operationalisation of Ganeshpur captive coal block. The Hon’ble Supreme Court, taking note of the fact that the Commission has already passed a consequential order dated 11.02.2026 for the implementation of the APTEL’s judgment dated 04.09.2025, directed the Commission to modify it in terms of the directions therein within four weeks from the date of the judgment. The relevant portion of the said judgment dated 27.02.2026 is extracted as under: _**26** . In light of such discussion, the appeals are partly allowed and the impugned order dated 04.09.2025 passed by APTEL is set aside to the limited extent that it grants compensation for procurement of coal through e- auction/import to meet shortfall in tapering linkage granted to it pending operationalization of the Ganeshpur captive coal block. The remaining portion of the order awarding compensation on account of Change in Law events with effect from 25.08.2014 along with carrying costs till the date of actual payment, is upheld. Though not placed on record during the course of hearing, we have taken note of the fact that CERC has already passed a consequential order dated 11.02.2026 for implementation of the impugned order. We direct CERC_ _to modify its order in terms of the aforesaid directions within four weeks from the date of this order. No order as to costs.”_ Court, the Commission hereby modifies its earlier order dated 11.02.2026 as under: 8. In terms of the above modifications to the order dated 11.02.2026, the direction of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the judgment dated 27.2.2026 stands implemented.
